score_rationale: The verified minimax characterization is substantial and potentially publishable, but the manuscript requires major revision to make its verification scope accurate, its load-bearing arguments reader-accessible, and its presentation suitable for a leading econometrics journal.
summary: The paper establishes a sharp finite-sample minimax risk for finite-alphabet ATE estimation with separate outcome-labeled and treatment-covariate samples, supported by a constructive hybrid estimator, a common-marginal converse, and known-marginal and sequence-regime consequences. The contribution is technically strong and well targeted to an important chart-review allocation problem. Publication requires substantial expository restructuring and correction of the verification disclosure, although the supplied verification contract supports the principal mathematical claims.
strengths: The central rate sharply separates labeled-outcome information from pooled treatment-covariate information for all stated sample sizes and alphabet sizes.
The upper bound is constructive, and the comparison with the inverse-count baseline clearly identifies the logarithmic gain from polynomial correction in sparse cells.
The common-marginal lower-bound construction is well aligned with the two-sample experiment and delivers a conceptually informative converse.
The known-marginal limit and exact sequence criteria make the main frontier useful beyond a single asymptotic regime.
The related-work section engages the closest supervised discrete-covariate benchmark and situates the result within causal, semi-supervised, and discrete-functional estimation.
The limitations section candidly quantifies the impracticality of the proof-oriented finite calibration and states the model scope accurately.

findings.issue: The verification disclosure overstates and incompletely documents the formalization. It says, “The displayed definitions, assumptions, lemmas, propositions, and theorems in this paper ... form the machine-checked mathematical layer in Lean 4,” although numerous displayed definitions are explicitly presentation-synthesized rather than mapped to Lean declarations. The author footnote also promises a recorded toolchain and commit, but the verification note supplies neither the commit nor toolchain metadata.
findings.fix: Replace the blanket statement with an exact scope disclosure distinguishing mapped declarations and audited proofs from presentation-level definitions. Add the verified commit, Lean/toolchain versions, and a stable statement-to-declaration manifest, or remove the metadata promise from the author footnote.

findings.issue: Several load-bearing ingredients enter the reader-facing proofs only as unnamed assertions. Most importantly, the proof of the uniform-intensity construction invokes “the one-coordinate marked-Poisson moment-matching estimate” to obtain the exponential total-variation bound, which is the core indistinguishability step, without stating, proving, or citing that estimate. Similar hidden inputs include the “uniform calibration-failure bound” in the hybrid-risk proof and the “compact finite-model selection step” in the side-information argument.
findings.fix: State these inputs as clearly named lemmas with hypotheses and conclusions, supply concise proofs or precise citations, and cross-reference them at every use. At minimum, expose the exact one-coordinate likelihood or total-variation estimate and explain how moment matching yields the factor rho_epsilon^L.

findings.issue: The paper’s journal-facing argument is obscured by generated formal scaffolding. The Binary length definition contains a page-scale dependency list referencing many later objects, the main estimator definition embeds extensive proof-calibration constants, and the appendices reproduce very long certificate-level proofs without a concise statistical proof roadmap. This makes the substantive estimator and lower-bound ideas difficult to evaluate independently of the formal artifact.
findings.fix: Remove the dependency-record item from the reader-facing manuscript, move calibration certificates and full formal proof renderings to a separately identified supplement, and retain in the main paper a concise estimator definition, a theorem-level proof outline, and a dependency map organized by statistical ideas rather than generated object identifiers.

findings.issue: The displayed inverse-count prefix estimator divides by u=M_0/8 for every n>=1, while M_0=0 for n=1 and n=2. Ordinary mathematical notation therefore leaves the estimator undefined in part of the parameter range covered by the theorem, even though the verified implementation uses totalized real division.
findings.fix: State explicitly in the inverse-count definition that these divisions use the same totalized-real convention as the verified object, including the value when u=0. Explain briefly how this makes the clipped estimator well defined for the small-n cases handled by the theorem.

findings.issue: The closest-competitor comparison remains under-specified at precisely the point where novelty is claimed. Phrases such as “in the stated alphabet regime” omit that regime, and the external locators are written as “Theorems~1--2 of \citet{...}” and “discussion after Theorem~2” rather than being carried by the citation command.
findings.fix: Verify and state the exact sample-size and alphabet conditions for the cited upper and lower bounds, identify any differences in model class or loss, and use locator-bearing citations such as \citet[Theorems 1--2]{...} and the precise discussion locator.

findings.issue: The sentence “Appendix~B independently supplies the common-marginal converse” violates the paper’s cleveref-only cross-reference rule and risks becoming incorrect when appendices are reordered.
findings.fix: Replace the manual appendix reference with \cref{sec:appendix-lower} and audit the manuscript for any remaining manual internal kind or number references.

findings.issue: Two explanatory sentences violate the affirmative-framing contract outside the limitations section: “it imposes no additional statistical assumption” and “it is a mathematical totality claim, not a claim that the very conservative finite calibration is computationally practical.”
findings.fix: Rewrite affirmatively, for example: “The Context item records formal dependencies.” and “Here total computable means that the finite sums define an everywhere-defined statistic; the implementation-oriented scope is discussed in the Limitations and future work paragraph.”

findings.issue: The opening claim that the theorem “separates the annotation experiment into three interpretable regimes” suggests a partition, whereas consistency, parametric-rate behavior, and strict improvement are overlapping sequence properties with separate equivalence conditions.
findings.fix: Call them “three sequence consequences” or explicitly define a mutually exclusive regime partition before using the term “three regimes.”

findings.issue: The notation “\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}: \mathcal T_{n,m,d}” treats an estimator class as though it were a codomain or type, while the following display defines a map from the sample space to the reals.
findings.fix: Write the mapping signature explicitly and then state membership, for example \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}:\mathrm{Sample}(n,m,d)\to\mathbb R and, after measurability is established, \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}\in\mathcal T_{n,m,d}.

findings.issue: The comparison table has no caption, label, or explanatory reference in the surrounding prose, which weakens its role in the paper’s positioning argument.
findings.fix: Give the table a descriptive caption and label, reference it with cleveref, and add one sentence explaining the dimensions along which the four entries differ.

questions_for_authors: Where in the reader-accessible paper or supplement is the one-coordinate marked-Poisson moment-matching estimate that yields the rho_epsilon^L total-variation decay stated and proved?
Do the authors intend every division in the inverse-count estimator to use Lean’s totalized-real convention, particularly when n is 1 or 2?
Will the final reproducibility appendix include the exact commit, Lean/toolchain versions, and a manifest distinguishing mapped declarations from presentation-synthesized definitions?
